To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
fat-coated organic acids and a feed enzyme can be used as growth promotants in poultry nutrition.

the tested feed additives had no negative effect on broiler growth performance and nutrient utilization, but they affected the morphology of the small intestines and the microflora activity in the crop, the stomach and the caecum.
fatcoated organic acid preparations and feed enzyme may be used to improve the growth performance of broilers.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the effect of organic acids and a feed enzyme used in the form of fat-coated preparations on the morphology of the small intestines and on the performance and nutrient utilization of broiler chickens.
a new approach of using fat-coated organic acids and a feed enzyme in broiler nutrition.

the effects of two fat-coasted preparations of organic acids and a feed enzyme used as feed additives on the performance of broiler chickens, nutrient utilization, morphology of the small intestinal tract and microflora activity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
fatcoated organic acid preparations are not effective as growth promoters in broilers.

the fat-coated organic acids used did not have a beneficial effect on the performance of broiler chicks, whereas the feed enzyme had a positive effect on performance and digestibility of organic matter.
the tested organic acid salts did not improve the growth performance and nutrient utilization of chickens, but they had a positive effect on small intestinal morphology.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fatcoated blend G improved the morphology and nutrient utilization in broilers, while fat-coated SB and the feed enzyme did not affect intestinal morphology and nutrient digestibility.

fat-coated organic salts and feed enzymes are useful in the broiler nutrition, but the effect of their supplementation on the performance and health status of broiler chickens depends on their interaction.
fat-coated blend G and SB improved nutrient utilization and growth performance of broiler chickens, but the effects of both additives were not additive.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the addition of organic acids and enzyme to broiler diets can affect the growth performance of birds and the utilization of nutrients, as well as the activity of intestinal microflora, and the morphology of the small intestinal tract.
the addition of fat-coated blend G and SB to the diets of broiler chickens increased the villi width, depth of crypts, and the width of tunica muscularis in the jejunums of birds.
the addition of fat-coated sodium butyrade to the diet of broiler chickens has no effect on the morphology of the jejunums or ileums.
